text: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
Blessed is the one who cares for the poor; in the day of trouble the LORD will deliver him.
The LORD will guard him and keep him alive; he will be called blessed in the land. You will not hand him over to the craving of his enemies.
The LORD will sustain him on his sickbed; you will restore him from the bed where illness lays him low.
I said, "LORD, have mercy on me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against you."

versions.text: I said, "LORD, have mercy on me; heal me, for I have sinned against you."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "heal my soul" (נפשי). While "heal me" is defensible, the psalmist's specific plea for the healing of the whole person/life is lost; restoring "my soul" better reflects the text and reads well aloud.

text: My enemies say of me in malice: "When will he die, and his name perish?"

versions.text: My enemies speak of me with malice: "When will he die and his name be gone?"
versions.explanation: "his name be gone" is weaker than the Hebrew אבד (perish); "perish" preserves the stronger verb and gives a firmer cadence for reading aloud.

text: When one comes to see me, he speaks empty words while his heart gathers up mischief; then he goes outside and spreads it.

versions.text: When one comes to see me, he speaks empty words while his heart gathers up slander; then he goes outside and spreads it.
versions.explanation: אָוֶן means iniquity, mischief, or wickedness rather than specifically "slander"; a broader term is more accurate while keeping the flow.

text: All who hate me whisper together against me; they imagine the worst for me:
"A vile disease has fastened on him; now that he lies down, he will never rise again."

versions.text: "Something deadly has been poured into him; now that he is down, he will never rise again."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew דבר־בליעל is literally "a thing of Belial" — a deadly/vile affliction — and the second clause is "he who lies down"; the revision keeps the imagery closer to the Hebrew and reads more naturally.

text: Even my trusted friend, the one who ate my bread, has lifted his heel against me.
But you, LORD, have mercy on me; raise me up, that I may repay them.
By this I know that you delight in me: my enemy will not shout in triumph over me.

versions.text: By this I know that you delight in me: my enemy does not shout in triumph over me.
versions.explanation: The imperfect יריע here expresses confidence about the outcome; "will not" better conveys the assurance and matches the future-oriented tone of the surrounding verses.

text: As for me, you have upheld me in my integrity and set me in your presence forever.
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and amen.
